title: Runtime: add profile-aware admission control (SKU + memory headroom queue limits)
author: Marcus Reed
description:
Context
We’re rolling out the hardware tuning profile pack and we now have SKU-specific defaults for batching, scheduler behavior, and KV cache headroom. One gap: today the runtime still uses a mostly static queue/admission policy (with some per-deployment overrides). Under bursty or mixed workloads, that can push certain SKUs (notably L40S, and some H100 configs with larger KV cache reservations) into allocator fragmentation/OOM territory and/or trigger p99 regressions due to queueing.

This PR introduces “profile-aware admission control”: admission and queue limits are derived from the active profile + detected GPU SKU + computed memory headroom, with explicit guardrails and observability.

What changed
- New AdmissionController that computes effective limits at startup and refreshes on model load/reload:
  - max_queue_requests
  - max_queue_tokens (prefill)
  - max_inflight_prefill
  - max_inflight_decode
  - max_concurrent_sequences
- Limits are derived from:
  - sku (H100 / L40S / B200)
  - active profile fields: kv_cache_reserved_bytes, allocator_headroom_ratio, scheduler_mode, and (optional) max_concurrency_cap
  - runtime-observed memory budget (cuda total mem) with a conservative safety margin
- Rejection/backpressure behavior:
  - If queue is full: return 429 (Too Many Requests) with Retry-After (ms) when we can estimate drain time; otherwise 503
  - If headroom is below the “safe” threshold for the configured profile: clamp limits further and emit a structured log at WARN once per 60s
- Added metrics (tagged with profile_id + sku):
  - runtime_admission_reject_total{reason}
  - runtime_admission_effective_limit{limit_name}
  - runtime_admission_clamp_events_total{cause}

Design notes / rationale
- We intentionally do NOT make this fully dynamic on a per-request basis (no feedback loop controller in v1). The goal is stable, deterministic limits per profile, with conservative clamping when we detect the configured headroom assumptions don’t match observed memory.
- The main driver for per-SKU behavior is that L40S has much tighter memory headroom and a higher incidence of allocator fragmentation under bursty prefill-heavy traffic. We clamp prefill inflight first, then queue tokens, then global concurrency.
- B200 is treated as “strict opt-in”: if the SKU is detected but the profile is marked preview/unsafe, we keep current static limits (and emit a WARN) unless the feature flag is explicitly enabled for that pool.

Rollout plan
- Behind feature flag: runtime.admission_control.profile_aware (default: false)
- Hosted: enable on H100 canary cohort first (5%), then L40S small cohort once metrics look healthy
- Dedicated/Private: keep disabled by default until we publish the expected behavior docs + rollout runbook (ENG-4933)

How to validate
- Unit tests cover:
  - deterministic limit calculation for H100/L40S given profile headroom values
  - clamp behavior when observed free memory < expected headroom
  - rejection status code mapping (429 vs 503) and Retry-After behavior
- Ran benchmark-lab “mixed” bucket (short prefill + long decode mix) on H100 and L40S:
  - H100: no measurable throughput regression; p99 improved ~4–7% due to lower queueing under burst
  - L40S: reduced OOM incidence in stress harness; p99 stable within noise with slightly lower peak throughput (expected)

Risks
- Too aggressive clamping could reduce peak throughput in some steady-state workloads. This is mitigated by SKU-specific defaults and the feature flag.
- Potential cardinality increase for new metrics: metrics are tagged only with sku + profile_id (no pool_id).

Follow-ups
- ENG-4930: wire these signals into perf-canary gates (block if clamp events spike or reject rate > threshold)
- ENG-4932: include these limits in “expected behavior” docs per SKU

Screenshots/Logs
- Example startup log (structured):
  admission_control.enabled=true sku=H100 profile_id=h100-default-v1 effective_limits={queue_tokens:32000,inflight_prefill:6,inflight_decode:12,concurrency:24} clamp=false

Checklist
- [x] Added tests
- [x] Added metrics + documentation comments
- [x] Feature flagged and safe default off
- [x] Reviewed with SRE for rollout semantics
commits: runtime/admission: introduce AdmissionController and integrate with scheduler queue
profiles: expose kv_cache_reserved_bytes + allocator_headroom_ratio via runtime ProfileView
metrics: add runtime_admission_* metrics (rejects, limits, clamps)
tests: add unit tests for effective limit calculation and clamping
docs: inline config docs for runtime.admission_control.profile_aware
review_conversation: Sofia Ivanova (review): Can you clarify ordering of clamps? I’d like to ensure we reduce prefill pressure before touching decode inflight, otherwise we might harm steady-state decode throughput.
Marcus Reed (author): Good call. Updated clamp ordering to: inflight_prefill -> queue_tokens -> global concurrency -> inflight_decode (last resort). Added a unit test asserting ordering.

Omar El-Sayed (review): The headroom math should account for kv_cache_reserved_bytes and allocator safety margin separately; right now it double-counts the margin in one branch. Also please emit a counter when clamping happens so we can alert on it.

Marcus Reed (author): Fixed double-count (now: expected_free = total - kv_reserved - weights_estimate - misc_margin; clamp_threshold uses allocator_headroom_ratio). Added runtime_admission_clamp_events_total{cause=headroom_mismatch|profile_cap}.
Neha Kapoor (review): For Hosted rollout, returning 429 seems fine, but we should ensure clients can distinguish it from rate limiting. Can we add an error code field in the response payload?
Marcus Reed (author): Added error.code = "admission_queue_full" and a short message; keeps existing HTTP status. Also included Retry-After only for queue_full (not for headroom clamp).
Allison Grant (review): Metric names look good. Please confirm tags are only sku + profile_id; don’t add pool_id or model_id.
Marcus Reed (author): Confirmed. No additional high-cardinality labels. Added a comment in registry_runtime.cc to prevent future additions without review.
Sean Gallagher (review): Can we ensure this stays off by default everywhere including Private installs? Also: what’s the kill switch story if reject rates spike during canary?

Marcus Reed (author): Flag default is false in runtime_flags.yaml; Helm/installer inherit. Kill switch is disabling runtime.admission_control.profile_aware via dynamic config and restarting pods (same mechanism as other runtime flags). Noted in description.
Sofia Ivanova (approval): Approved after clamp ordering + tests.
Neha Kapoor (approval): Approved. Please link this in the rollout runbook once it’s created.
release_notes:
- Adds optional profile-aware admission control to prevent overload by clamping queue/inflight limits based on GPU SKU and memory headroom.
- Exposes new runtime_admission_* metrics tagged by sku and profile_id for rollout monitoring.
